# kuro-plugins

> The plugin platform for Yorozo (dazacode/yorozo-client): the SDK a plugin imports,
> the `kuro` CLI, and the plugins themselves. A plugin teaches Yorozo about a content
> source it did not know about. The plugin supplies data; the host supplies experience.
>
> `kuro` is the identifier everywhere — the CLI, `@kuro/plugin-sdk`, the
> `app.kuro.plugins.*` namespace. Yorozo is the product a viewer sees, so a packaged
> plugin is a `.yorozoplugin`, which is what the client's installer accepts.

A plugin is one ES module with a default export answering three methods:
`searchCatalog(query, page, ctx, cursor?)`, `listEpisodes(sourceMediaId, ctx)` and
`resolve(sourceMediaId, episode, ctx)`. It has no ambient capabilities — no `fetch`,
no DOM, no filesystem, no timers held across calls. Everything it can do arrives as
`ctx`, and every hostname it reaches must be declared in `plugin.json` under
`network.hosts` or the request throws before a packet leaves.

Four rules the design turns on, and none of them are style preferences:

1. **You never send a request.** `ctx.http` does, only to declared hosts.
2. **You never draw UI.** You declare `settings` as data; the host renders them on
   all six platforms.
3. **You never touch a segment.** When a stream is not playable as served you
   *describe* the repair as ops and the host executes it natively — because one
   bundle runs on three JS engines and passing hundreds of multi-megabyte buffers
   across an FFI boundary is ruinous on a phone and invisible on a laptop.
4. **Missing data is an event, not a value.** Throw `NotFoundError` or
   `SourceChangedError`. An empty list makes a broken plugin look exactly like a
   show with no episodes, which is the failure this project exists to eliminate.

Development never involves the app — no Flutter, no simulator, no device. Tests
record real traffic once into committed cassettes and replay them offline in about
a hundred milliseconds, so a source changing becomes a failing test with a diff
rather than a black screen reported weeks later.

## Writing a plugin

- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): four paths, by what you are doing.
- [Your first plugin](docs/first-plugin.md): `kuro new` to a signed `.yorozoplugin`, including the cassette idiom that `save()` depends on.
- [The manifest](docs/manifest.md): every field, why `network.hosts` is enforced rather than advisory, and how to prove a setting is actually read.
- [The three methods](docs/three-methods.md): signatures, `CatalogPage.hasMore`, the error vocabulary, `PlaybackSource`, and the declarative byte pipeline.
- [When it goes wrong](docs/troubleshooting.md): the real error strings and what each means.
- [Porting an existing extension](docs/porting.md): for people arriving with an extension rather than an empty directory.
- [Plugin repositories](docs/repository.md): `index.json`, signing, installing, updates, trust.

## Read the reference plugin

[`plugins/example/src/index.ts`](plugins/example/src/index.ts) talks to a fictional
API shaped like the awkward real ones — cursor-ish pagination, a separate call for
servers, config wedged into a `<script>` tag as not-quite-JSON, and a CDN that
disguises its segments. It is fully offline and commented as it goes.
[`plugins/example/test/example.spec.ts`](plugins/example/test/example.spec.ts) is the
suite shape to copy, including the test most people skip: executing the declared
pipeline against a recorded segment.

## The CLI

```
kuro new <name>                 scaffold
kuro test <plugin> [--record]   replay the tapes; --record refreshes them
kuro validate <plugin>          check the manifest and layout
kuro bundle <plugin>            build the single ES module the host loads
kuro package <plugin> [--key]   write a deterministic .yorozoplugin
kuro verify <archive> [--key]   check integrity, and signature if a key is given
kuro index --base-url <url>     write dist/index.json for a repository
kuro keygen                     make an Ed25519 signing key pair
```

## Layout

- `packages/kuro-plugin-sdk/` — what a plugin imports: types, `ctx`, extraction helpers, pipeline ops, the test harness.
- `packages/kuro-plugin-tools/` — the `kuro` CLI. A developer dependency; never reaches a device.
- `schema/`, `fixtures/` — copies of kuro's `contract/`, with a spec that alarms when a copy goes stale.

## If you already have a plugin for another ecosystem

[dazacode/plugin-bridge-js](https://github.com/dazacode/plugin-bridge-js) (Apache-2.0)
translates extensions written for Aniyomi, Stremio, Sora, Hayase, Mangayomi and Nuvio
into this same ABI, statically — no Android runtime, no bytecode interpreter.
`plugin-bridge check <dir|url>` translates one, runs it, and names what stopped it.
A translated plugin and one written here are the same artifact by the time a client
sees them, so this is worth trying before porting by hand.

It is also the reference implementation of the ABI — the sandbox, the host port, the
packager and the five-step conformance run — and therefore where to look when you need
to know exactly what a host does with what you return. Nothing in it is a prerequisite
for writing a plugin here.

## The client

[dazacode/yorozo-client](https://github.com/dazacode/yorozo-client) is the host: it
installs `.yorozoplugin` archives, renders the settings a manifest declares, executes
the byte pipeline a `resolve` describes, and ships no sources of its own.
